# Setup

```{r}

# Load packages
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(knitr)
library(readxl)
library(patchwork)

# Load data
exposure <- read.csv("ExposureConcentrationsRaw.csv")
# Loading in dataset with urban/rural classification for each county in NC 
urban_rural <- read_excel("urban_rural.xlsx")
# dataset with unemployment and median family income 
census <- read_excel("census_combined.xlsx")


```

## Data Tidying & Wrangling Code

#### Exposure Data

```{r}

# Select columns and rename for clarity
exposure_df <- exposure %>%
  select(County, Population, Pollutant.Name, Total.Exposure.Conc,
         OR.LightDuty.OffNetwork.Gas.Exposure.Conc,
         OR.LightDuty.OffNetwork.Diesel.Exposure.Conc,
         OR.HeavyDuty.OffNetwork.Gas.Exposure.Conc,
         OR.HeavyDuty.OffNetwork.Diesel.Exposure.Conc,
         OR.HeavyDuty.OnNetwork.Diesel.Exposure.Conc,
         OR.LightDuty.OnNetwork.Gas.Exposure.Conc,
         OR.LightDuty.OnNetwork.Diesel.Exposure.Conc,
         OR.HeavyDuty.OnNetwork.Gas.Exposure.Conc,
         OR.HeavyDuty.Hoteling.Exposure.Conc,
         OR.Refueling.Exposure.Conc,
         NR.Recreational.inc.PleasureCraft.Exposure.Conc,
         NR.Construction.Exposure.Conc,
         NR.Agriculture.Exposure.Conc,
         NR.CommercialEquipment.Exposure.Conc,
         NR.Locomotives.Exposure.Conc,
         NR.Point.Airports.Exposure.Conc,
         NR..Point.Railyards.Exposure.Conc) %>%
  rename("OR.Light.Off.Gas" = OR.LightDuty.OffNetwork.Gas.Exposure.Conc,
         "OR.Light.Off.Diesel" = OR.LightDuty.OffNetwork.Diesel.Exposure.Conc,
         "OR.Heavy.Off.Gas" = OR.HeavyDuty.OffNetwork.Gas.Exposure.Conc,
         "OR.Heavy.Off.Diesel" = OR.HeavyDuty.OffNetwork.Diesel.Exposure.Conc,
         "OR.Light.On.Gas" = OR.LightDuty.OnNetwork.Gas.Exposure.Conc,
         "OR.Light.On.Diesel" = OR.LightDuty.OnNetwork.Diesel.Exposure.Conc,
         "OR.Heavy.On.Gas" = OR.HeavyDuty.OnNetwork.Gas.Exposure.Conc,
         "OR.Heavy.On.Diesel" = OR.HeavyDuty.OnNetwork.Diesel.Exposure.Conc,
         "OR.Heavy.Idling" = OR.HeavyDuty.Hoteling.Exposure.Conc,
         "OR.Refueling" = OR.Refueling.Exposure.Conc,
         "NR.Recreational.Vehicles" = 
           NR.Recreational.inc.PleasureCraft.Exposure.Conc,
         "NR.Construction" = NR.Construction.Exposure.Conc,
         "NR.Agriculture" = NR.Agriculture.Exposure.Conc,
         "NR.Commerical.Equip" = NR.CommercialEquipment.Exposure.Conc,
         "NR.Locomotives" = NR.Locomotives.Exposure.Conc,
         "NR.Airpoints" = NR.Point.Airports.Exposure.Conc,
         "NR.Railyards" = NR..Point.Railyards.Exposure.Conc) %>%
  mutate(County = as.factor(County))

```

#### Urban/Rural & Census Data 

```{r}
# Making rural/urban data into a factor 
urban_rural$URBAN_RURAL <- as.factor(urban_rural$URBAN_RURAL)
# Filtering census data 
census_select <- census %>% 
  select(County, 
         `Median Family Income (Dollars)`:
           `Population Density (Persons Per SqMile)`)
# Making income a numeric class 
census_select$`Median Family Income (Dollars)` <- as.numeric(gsub("[^0-9]", "", 
                                census_select$`Median Family Income (Dollars)`))
census_select$`Population Density (Persons Per SqMile)` <-  as.numeric(gsub("[^0-9.]", "", census_select$`Population Density (Persons Per SqMile)`))
```

#### Formaldehyde Data

```{r}

formaldehyde <- exposure_df %>% 
  filter(Pollutant.Name == "FORMALDEHYDE") %>% 
  group_by(County) %>% 
  summarise(across(where(is.numeric), sum, na.rm = TRUE)) %>% 
  ungroup()
# subtracting entire state
formaldehyde <- formaldehyde[-34,]
# adding columns that sum all of the nonroad and onroad exposures for each county 
# formaldehyde dataframe still has all of the exposure activities so it can be 
# used for other analysis if we want 
formaldehyde <- formaldehyde %>% 
  mutate(Onroad_total = select(., OR.Light.Off.Gas:OR.Refueling) %>% 
      rowSums(na.rm = TRUE)) %>% 
  mutate(Nonroad_total = select(., NR.Recreational.Vehicles:NR.Railyards) %>% 
      rowSums(na.rm = TRUE)) 

# joining urban/rural column 
formaldehyde_select <- left_join(formaldehyde, urban_rural, by = "County")
# selecting necessary columns 
formaldehyde_select <- formaldehyde_select %>% 
  select(County, Population, Total.Exposure.Conc, Onroad_total:URBAN_RURAL) 
# joining with census data 
formaldehyde_complete <- left_join(formaldehyde_select, 
                                   census_select, by = "County")
# making county into factor
formaldehyde_complete$County <- as.factor(formaldehyde_complete$County)

```

#### Benzene Data

```{r}

benzene <- exposure_df %>% 
  filter(Pollutant.Name == "BENZENE") %>% 
  group_by(County) %>% 
  summarise(across(where(is.numeric), sum, na.rm = TRUE)) %>% 
  ungroup()
# subtracting entire state
benzene <- benzene[-34,]
# adding columns that sum all of the nonroad and onroad exposures for each county 
benzene <- benzene %>% 
  mutate(Onroad_total = select(., OR.Light.Off.Gas:OR.Refueling) %>% 
           rowSums(na.rm = TRUE)) %>% 
  mutate(Nonroad_total = select(., NR.Recreational.Vehicles:NR.Railyards) %>% 
           rowSums(na.rm = TRUE)) 

# joining urban/rural column 
benzene_select <- left_join(benzene, urban_rural, by = "County")
# selecting necessary columns 
benzene_select <- benzene_select %>% 
  select(County, Population, Total.Exposure.Conc, Onroad_total:URBAN_RURAL) 
# joining with census data 
benzene_complete <- left_join(benzene_select, census_select, by = "County") 
# making county into factor 
benzene_complete$County <- as.factor(benzene_complete$County)

```

#### Diesel Data

```{r}

## Diesel 
diesel <- exposure_df %>% 
  filter(Pollutant.Name == "DIESEL PM") %>% 
  group_by(County) %>% 
  summarise(across(where(is.numeric), sum, na.rm = TRUE)) %>% 
  ungroup()
# subtracting entire state
diesel <- diesel[-34,]
# adding columns that sum all of the nonroad and onroad exposures for each county 
diesel <- diesel %>% 
  mutate(
    Onroad_total = 
      select(., OR.Light.Off.Gas:OR.Refueling) %>% 
      rowSums(na.rm = TRUE)) %>% 
  mutate(Nonroad_total = select(., NR.Recreational.Vehicles:NR.Railyards) %>% 
           rowSums(na.rm = TRUE)) 

# joining urban/rural column 
diesel_select <- left_join(diesel, urban_rural, by = "County")
# selecting necessary columns 
diesel_select <- diesel_select %>% 
  select(County, Population, Total.Exposure.Conc, Onroad_total:URBAN_RURAL)
  
# joining with census data 
diesel_complete <- left_join(diesel_select, census_select, by = "County") 
diesel_complete$County <- as.factor(diesel_complete$County)

## Can still join the cancer data in if we want to 

```

#### Formaldehyde Model 

```{r}

# Visualizing the relationship between response and descriptor variables 
(scatter_population <- ggplot(formaldehyde_complete, 
                              aes(x = Population, y = Total.Exposure.Conc)) + 
  geom_point() + 
   labs(x = "Population", 
        y = "ug/m3"))

(scatter_income <- ggplot(formaldehyde_complete, 
                          aes(x = `Median Family Income (Dollars)`, 
                              y = Total.Exposure.Conc)) + 
    geom_point() + 
    labs(x = "Median Family Income ($)", 
        y = "ug/m3"))

(scatter_urban <- ggplot(formaldehyde_complete, 
                         aes(x = URBAN_RURAL, y = Total.Exposure.Conc)) + 
    geom_point() + 
    labs(x = "Urban or Rural Designation", 
        y = "ug/m3"))

(scatter_density <- ggplot(formaldehyde_complete, 
                           aes(x = `Population Density (Persons Per SqMile)`, 
                               y = Total.Exposure.Conc)) +
    geom_point() + 
    labs(x = "Population Density (Persons/sqMile)", 
        y = "ug/m3"))

(scatter_unemployment <- ggplot(formaldehyde_complete, 
                                aes(x =`Unemployment(Percent)`, 
                                    y = Total.Exposure.Conc)) + 
    geom_point() + 
    labs(x = "Unemployment (%)", 
        y = "ug/m3"))

final_plot <- ((scatter_density + scatter_urban) / 
  (scatter_population + scatter_unemployment) / scatter_income) + 
  plot_annotation(title = "Formaldehyde Concentrations vs. County Demographics")
plot(final_plot)

# Perform correlation tests to test for collinearity

cor.test(formaldehyde_complete$Population, 
         formaldehyde_complete$`Median Family Income (Dollars)`) 
# p < 0.01, cor = 0.4802

cor.test(formaldehyde_complete$Population, 
         formaldehyde_complete$`Population Density (Persons Per SqMile)`) 
# p < 0.01, cor = 0.9144

cor.test(formaldehyde_complete$`Unemployment(Percent)`, 
         formaldehyde_complete$`Median Family Income (Dollars)`)
# p < 0.01, cor = -0.4911

cor.test(formaldehyde_complete$`Median Family Income (Dollars)`,
         formaldehyde_complete$`Population Density (Persons Per SqMile)`)
# p < 0.01, cor = 0.402

# Generate regression model(s)
F_model1 <- lm(Total.Exposure.Conc ~ Population + URBAN_RURAL, 
               formaldehyde_complete)
summary(F_model1)
plot(F_model1)

F_model2 <- lm(Total.Exposure.Conc ~ `Population Density (Persons Per SqMile)` + 
                 URBAN_RURAL, formaldehyde_complete)
summary(F_model2)
plot(F_model2)

formaldehyde_nooutlier <- formaldehyde_complete[-92,]
formaldehyde_nooutlier <- formaldehyde_nooutlier[-60,]
model1_nooutlier <- lm(Total.Exposure.Conc ~ Population + URBAN_RURAL, 
                       formaldehyde_nooutlier)
summary(model1_nooutlier)
plot(model1_nooutlier)

model2_nooutlier <- lm(Total.Exposure.Conc ~ 
                         `Population Density (Persons Per SqMile)` + 
                         URBAN_RURAL, formaldehyde_nooutlier)
summary(model2_nooutlier)
plot(model2_nooutlier)

model3 <- lm(Total.Exposure.Conc ~ URBAN_RURAL + 
               `Median Family Income (Dollars)` + 
               Population, formaldehyde_nooutlier)
summary(model3)
plot(model3)

AIC1 <- AIC(model1_nooutlier)
AIC2 <- AIC(model2_nooutlier)
AIC3 <- AIC(model3)

# Model 1 without outliers has the lowest AIC value and is the one that I will write the results about. 

```
